inclusion.I3: Functional MRI (fMRI) or positron emission tomography (PET) studies
inclusion.I4: Studies examining executive function or cognitive control tasks

inclusion.I5: Functional MRI (fMRI) or positron emission tomography (PET) study assessing executive function or cognitive control using a task-based paradigm
inclusion.I6: Tasks must fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation)
inclusion.I7: Whole-brain evidence- at least one analysis must be a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. Partial-brain acquisition (e.g. limited slice coverage) still qualifies, so long as the analysis was voxelwise rather than confined to a priori regions.
inclusion.I8: At least one analysis must be a WITHIN-GROUP task contrast. The comparison condition may be an active control task, or an implicit baseline, rest or fixation- a main effect of task against implicit baseline qualifies.
inclusion.I9: Any participant group qualifies, including clinical samples (e.g. schizophrenia, depression) and developmental samples (e.g. adolescents), provided a within-group task contrast is reported for at least one group. Do not exclude a study because of who its participants were, or because it does not state their ages.
inclusion.I10: It is acceptable for qualifying whole-brain results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials, as long as they are clearly described in the text.

exclusion.E3: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) or small-volume-corrected analyses with no voxelwise results.
exclusion.E4: Studies that report only connectivity analyses (e.g., functional connectivity, PPI, DCM) or resting-state analyses without also reporting a task activation map.
exclusion.E5: Studies that report ONLY between-group contrasts (e.g., patient vs control, adults vs adolescents) or group x condition interactions, with no within-group task activation contrast for any group. Note this is about the contrast, not the sample- a within-group contrast computed in a patient or adolescent sample qualifies.
exclusion.E6: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original human neuroimaging data.

inclusion.GLOBAL_I1: Scope- You are judging ONE analysis, not the paper. The study text is provided only to interpret this analysis. That the paper elsewhere reports a qualifying contrast is not by itself a reason to include this analysis.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I2: How to read the analysis- Judge it from its name, its description and its table caption together. An empty or uninformative analysis name (e.g. "analysis_0") usually means the analysis is the only one in its table, in which case the caption describes it fully and you should judge from the caption. A blank name is never itself a reason to exclude.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I3: The analysis must be a within-group, group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrast.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I4: Sample- Any participant group qualifies, including clinical samples (e.g. schizophrenia, depression) and developmental samples (e.g. adolescents), so long as the contrast is computed WITHIN a group rather than between groups. Do not exclude an analysis because of who the participants were.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I5: Baseline- The comparison condition may be an active control task, or an implicit baseline, rest or fixation. A main effect of task against implicit baseline qualifies. Do not require an active control condition.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I6: Response mode- The task may require an overt behavioral response (e.g. a button press) or a covert one (e.g. silent naming or counting). Do not require an overt response.

exclusion.GLOBAL_E1: Group-comparison contrasts- an analysis whose contrast is between two participant groups (e.g. patients vs controls, adults vs adolescents) or a group x condition interaction. Note this is about the CONTRAST, not the sample: a within-group contrast computed in a patient or adolescent sample is eligible.
exclusion.GLOBAL_E3: Connectivity or resting-state analyses (functional connectivity, PPI, DCM, ICA)
exclusion.GLOBAL_E4: The analysis does not reflect an executive function task contrast at all (e.g. a motor or sensory localiser, a physiological or artefact regressor, or a purely structural result).

inclusion.POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I1: The task belongs to any of the six executive function domains: flexibility, inhibition, working memory, initiation, planning, or vigilance
inclusion.POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I2: The contrast reflects the executive demand of that task (this includes a main effect of the task against implicit baseline, not only task-versus-active-control contrasts)

inclusion.WORKING_MEMORY_I1: Task is a WORKING MEMORY paradigm: n-back, AX-CPT, Sternberg task, delayed match-to-sample, spatial span or sequence recall, or complex calculation/PASAT
inclusion.WORKING_MEMORY_I2: The contrast reflects memory load, maintenance or manipulation (e.g. 2-back > 0-back, high load > low load, main effect of delay, a linear regression on load, or an encoding or retrieval main effect)

exclusion.WORKING_MEMORY_E1: The contrast being annotated isolates a different executive function domain (e.g., Go/No-Go, Stroop, task switching, Tower tasks, word generation, oddball). Other tasks reported elsewhere in the same paper are irrelevant: judge only the contrast described by this analysis.

inclusion.INHIBITION_I1: Task is an INHIBITION paradigm: Go/No-Go, Stroop, Flanker, Simon task, or antisaccade
inclusion.INHIBITION_I2: The contrast reflects the inhibitory demand (e.g. No-Go > Go, incongruent > congruent, antisaccade > prosaccade, or a No-Go or Stroop main effect against implicit baseline)

exclusion.INHIBITION_E1: The contrast being annotated isolates a different executive function domain (e.g., n-back, Sternberg, task switching, Tower tasks, word generation, oddball). Other tasks reported elsewhere in the same paper are irrelevant: judge only the contrast described by this analysis.

inclusion.COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I1: Task is a FLEXIBILITY paradigm: task switching or the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test
inclusion.COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I2: The contrast reflects the switching demand (e.g. switch trials > repeat trials, set-shifting > maintenance, or a switching main effect)

exclusion.COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_E1: The contrast being annotated isolates a different executive function domain (e.g., n-back, Go/No-Go, Stroop, Tower tasks, word generation, oddball). Other tasks reported elsewhere in the same paper are irrelevant: judge only the contrast described by this analysis.

inclusion.PLANNING_I1: Task is a PLANNING paradigm: Tower Maze test, Tower of London, or Tower of Hanoi
inclusion.PLANNING_I2: The contrast reflects planning demand (e.g. high-move > low-move planning problems, or a planning main effect)

exclusion.PLANNING_E1: The contrast being annotated isolates a different executive function domain (e.g., n-back, Go/No-Go, Stroop, task switching, word generation, oddball). Other tasks reported elsewhere in the same paper are irrelevant: judge only the contrast described by this analysis.

inclusion.VIGILANCE_I1: Task is a VIGILANCE paradigm: oddball discrimination, or an equivalent task requiring set maintenance while resisting interference
inclusion.VIGILANCE_I2: The contrast reflects the demand to maintain set (e.g. target > standard stimuli, or a target-detection main effect)

exclusion.VIGILANCE_E1: The contrast being annotated isolates a different executive function domain (e.g., n-back, Go/No-Go, Stroop, task switching, Tower tasks, word generation). Other tasks reported elsewhere in the same paper are irrelevant: judge only the contrast described by this analysis.

inclusion.INITIATION_I1: Task is an INITIATION paradigm: word generation or verbal fluency
inclusion.INITIATION_I2: The contrast reflects self-initiated generation (e.g. word generation > word repetition, or a generation main effect). Covert or silent generation qualifies.

exclusion.INITIATION_E1: The contrast being annotated isolates a different executive function domain (e.g., n-back, Go/No-Go, Stroop, task switching, Tower tasks, oddball). Other tasks reported elsewhere in the same paper are irrelevant: judge only the contrast described by this analysis.
